- Constraints: strict JSON validation, low-latency callpaths for live UI, and integration with your existing auth model.

Proposed next steps
1) I attached a SOW draft and a sample structured-output schema (see attachments). Please review the schema and call out any required fields we missed.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Aditya (solutions) and Dylan (engineer) to walk SDK setup, auth, routing, and decoding/validation patterns. Proposed slots: Tue 6/30 1:30pm or Wed 7/1 10:00am PT — let me know what works.
3) John: can you confirm the expected max tokens per response and whether you need strictly schema-only responses (i.e. model should never emit freeform text)? That will drive our recommended guardrails.

Pre-read / quick answers
- Constrained decoding: We recommend a two-layer approach: 1) use function-calling/structured output features (Redwood function/tool calling or model's function calling) to reduce freeform tokens, and 2) enforce a post-generation JSON schema validation step.
- Retry patterns: detect invalid JSON -> run a single automatic correction pass (prompted parse-fixer) -> if still invalid, fallback to a strict-temperature regeneration with explicit instructions to only output JSON. We'll share code snippets in the deep-dive.
- Embeddings/reranking: for interactive UIs we recommend small batches (<=16) with async prefetching and a local L2 cache on the client for top-k hits. We'll cover throughput numbers in the call and map them to your SLA.

Subject: Deep-dive notes: SDK/auth, routing, structured-output reliability patterns

Hi John / ACME team — looping in some concrete patterns we typically share during the technical deep-dive. We'll walk these live, but sharing in writing so you have something to reference ahead of the call.

1) SDK setup & auth - Initialize client with an API key stored in env (best for hosted):

  // pseudo-code (JS)
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
  const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })

- For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed mTLS or API keys issued per-service account. If you move to private, we recommend using mTLS + short-lived certs for service-to-service calls.
- Token rotation: use short-lived tokens where possible and store secrets in a KMS.

2) Routing & model selection - Use request-level routing metadata to pick the model variant for reliability vs cost:
- header: X-Redwood-Model: redwood-struct-v1 (strict decoder profile)
- fallback policy: if timed out or capacity constrained, route to redwood-struct-v1-lite with same schema but smaller context window.

3) Structured output (schema + constrained decoding)
- Primary strategy: function-calling/structured-output API to force a typed response. Provide a JSON Schema (attached: structured-output-schema.json) with required fields and types.
- Secondary safety net: server-side validator (we recommend Ajv for JS) that verifies schema conformance immediately on response.

Example validation flow
1) Call model with structured-output schema + low temperature (0–0.2).
2) Validate JSON with Ajv (or equivalent).
3) If invalid:
   a) Run a single automatic repair pass: re-prompt the model with the original output and instruction: "Only return valid JSON that conforms to the schema. Here is the invalid JSON: <...>. Fix it."
   b) Validate repaired JSON.
   c) If still invalid after 1 repair, trigger fallback: call model with an even stricter system prompt + function-calling and higher sampling attempts (up to N=2) before surfacing an error to the client.

Idempotency & retries - Mark each request with an idempotency key so retries don't double-process downstream writes. If you must retry, prefer client-side exponential backoff (jitter) and server-side request deduplication keyed by idempotency token.

Partial / truncated responses - Monitor token usage / termination reason. If generation truncated (e.g., max tokens), re-invoke with increased max_tokens and explicit instruction to only return the missing top-level fields.

Embeddings & rerankers - Throughput guidance: for sub-200ms p95 you typically need a dedicated pool and batching size tuned to your latency SLO. We recommend:
  - Small batches (8–16) for real-time paths
  - Background reindexing with larger batches for offline pipelines
- Reranker pattern: generate a candidate set with retrieval, then call a high-precision reranker model with structured score outputs (rank and confidence). Keep reranker calls synchronous but small-batched.

Attachments referenced in this thread:
- structured-output-schema.json (sample schema)
- sdk-snippets.txt (small auth/routing snippets)

I'll bring a few sample validators and a short demo of the repair pass. If you want, I can paste the Ajv schema snippet into the shared Drive before the call — say the word and I'll upload.
